questions.knowledge_point: Calculating Flux Across the Surface of a Known Solid
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096233/assets/d0f6f5ed91981e15d2fb80e2630cec6d20f566feb627899f529e07bab12b73fb.png)

Consider the vector field $F=⟨{z}^{2},\,2y,\,{x}^{2}+y⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by the bounding region of a right circular cylinder of height $2$ whose base is a circle of radius $1$ centered at the origin, as shown above. Given that $S$ is positively (outward) oriented, use the divergence theorem to find the flux of $F$ through $S.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({z}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y)+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}+y) \\  & =0+2+0 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid cylinder enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}2\,\text{d}V \\  & =2{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =2\cdot \text{Volume}(R) \\  & =2\cdot \pi \cdot {1}^{2}\cdot 2 \\  & =4\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.

\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(1-2x)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(5y-3{z}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{3}-{y}^{2}) \\  & =-2+5+0 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}

Given that $S$ is positively (outward) oriented, use the divergence theorem to find the flux of $F$ through $S.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3x-y{z}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(y+{e}^{z})+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2y\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =3+1+0 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the rectangular solid enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}4\,\text{d}V \\  & =4{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =4\cdot \text{Volume}(R) \\  & =4\cdot 1\cdot 2\cdot 1 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating Flux Across a Closed Surface
questions.problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=1,$ $x=3,$ $y=0,$ $y=2,$ $z=-1,$ $z=1.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=(y-{x}^{2})\,i+xy\,j+3xz\,k,$ find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-{x}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(3xz) \\  & =(-2x)+x+3x \\  & =2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}2x\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}2x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}2x\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}z \\  & =[{x}^{2}]_{x=1}^{x=3}\cdot (2-0)\cdot (1-(-1)) \\  & =(9-1)\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =32.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=-1,$ $x=1,$ $y=0,$ $y=3,$ $z=1,$ $z=3.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=(2{x}^{3}+z)\,i-z\,j-3{x}^{2}z\,k,$ find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{3}+z)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-z)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(-3{x}^{2}z) \\  & =6{x}^{2}+0+(-3{x}^{2}) \\  & =3{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{3}3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}3{x}^{2}\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{3}\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{1}^{3}\text{d}z \\  & =[{x}^{3}]_{x=-1}^{x=1}\cdot (3-0)\cdot (3-1) \\  & =({1}^{3}-(-1)^{3})\cdot 3\cdot 2 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$
